title: British unemployment and consumer-price inflation, annual, 1954-1986 (Chapter 44: the natural rate and the drifting Phillips curve)
source: Bank of England, 'A millennium of macroeconomic data for the UK' (version 3.1): sheets 'A47. Wages and prices' and 'A50. Employment & unemployment'
series: cpi_infl_pct: CPI inflation, GB/UK (GB+NI), annual inflation rate, per cent (A47, column 4; the change of the spliced index of column 3, whose heading names its sources: '1949-2014 CPI (ONS)' for these years); unemp_pct: the unemployment rate as a % of total UK workforce (A50, column 9), which is 100 x unemployed_000s / (employment_000s + unemployed_000s); unemployed_000s: unemployed, thousands, the preferred measure adjusting 1946-1971 data for LFS/CC differences in female unemployment (A50, column 6: from 1971 the ONS Labour Force Survey series MGSC; to 1970 the mid-year estimates of the Economic Trends Annual Supplement 1997 edition plus an adjustment scaled to match the LFS/claimant-count discrepancy in female unemployment); employment_000s: total employment in heads, thousands (A50, column 2: from 1971 the ONS Labour Force Survey series MGRZ; to 1970 chained back on the workforce in employment, mid-year estimates of the Economic Trends Annual Supplement 1997 edition)
license: The workbook's notes ask users of its sections to cite the underlying source ('When using this data, please cite this source.'). The Bank of England publishes it as a research dataset; a subset is stored here for teaching, with attribution to the Bank of England and to the sources its headings name for these years: the Office for National Statistics (the CPI from 1949; the Labour Force Survey series MGRZ and MGSC from 1971) and the Economic Trends Annual Supplement 1997 edition (the mid-year estimates of employment and unemployment before 1971).
notes: Workbook SHA-256 4c23dd392a498691eac92659aec283fb43f28118bd80511dc87fc595974195eb, the copy used for Chapters 19-38, downloaded again on 2026-11-12 with the same hash. The fetch script checks that column 4 of A47 is the change of the index of column 3, that column 9 of A50 is 100 x column 6 / (column 2 + column 6), that from 1971 columns 2 and 6 equal the LFS series MGRZ and MGSC (columns 62 and 68), and that before 1971 column 6 is the 1997 supplement's mid-year estimate (column 53) plus the female adjustment (column 104) while column 2 moves with the supplement's workforce in employment (column 49). The rate is not the claimant count that British governments published at the time. Chapter 44 draws 1955-1985 in Figure naturalrate_jpuk(a) and quotes the range of 1955-1969 and the years 1971, 1974, 1975, 1980, 1981 and 1983 in its text.
